title: Hip Osteoarthritis Relief in Sarasota, FL | MD Fit
h1: Hip Osteoarthritis Relief in Sarasota, FL
description: Hip osteoarthritis in Sarasota: groin ache, stiff mornings, trouble with socks. Dr. Jared Caban on the hip flexors and glutes that drive the pain.
lead: Hip arthritis rarely announces itself in the hip. It shows up as a groin ache, a stiff morning, difficulty putting on socks, and sometimes knee pain that no one can explain. Much of what hurts day to day is muscular, and that part responds to treatment.

sections.html:
The pain is usually in the groin or the front of the hip, sometimes wrapping to the outer hip or buttock, and in a surprising number of people it is felt mostly in the thigh or knee. Mornings are stiff. The first steps after sitting are the worst, then it eases, then it aches again after a long walk. Rotating the hip, crossing the legs, reaching the foot to tie a shoe, and getting in and out of the car become harder over time. Walking distance shrinks, a limp appears, and the leg may start to turn outward.

Like the knee, the amount of arthritis on an X-ray does not predict how much a hip hurts. Dr. Jared treats people with significant imaging who move well and others with mild changes who are in constant pain because the hip flexors and glutes have locked the joint down.

sections.h2: The muscles around a stiff hip
sections.html:
When a joint loses motion, the muscles around it shorten to match, and then they become a pain source of their own.

  • Iliacus and psoas are almost always short and tender in an arthritic hip. They refer a deep groin and front-pocket ache, pull the trunk forward so standing tall is hard, and make the first steps after sitting painful.
  • Gluteus medius and gluteus minimus weaken as walking changes. They refer along the belt line and down the outside of the leg, cause the lurching limp, and make lying on the side painful at night.
  • Tensor fasciae latae overworks when the glutes do not, producing front-outer hip pain down the thigh that is often labeled bursitis.
  • Adductor longus tightens with the loss of rotation and broadens the groin ache down the inner thigh.

Releasing these does not change the cartilage, but it changes how far the hip moves and how much it hurts, which is what most people actually want.

sections.h2: How MD Fit works with an arthritic hip
sections.html: Assessment looks at hip rotation and extension, how you walk, single-leg control, hip flexor length and which muscles reproduce your pain under pressure. Release of the hip flexors, TFL, glutes and adductors is hands-on and is often the first time in months the hip has felt loose. Correction centers on standing tall, walking with a longer step on the arthritic side, and using the hip rather than the low back to bend. Homework from the free MD Fit app includes videos such as Hip Neuroglide, Couch Stretch, Standing Clamshell and Glute Walk, chosen to fit your motion. Strengthening of the gluteals, trunk and legs then protects the joint and keeps you walking. Dr. Jared's training as a physician and clinical exercise physiologist means the loading is dosed carefully, and if a hip replacement is eventually the right call, you go into it strong and come out of it faster.

• Stand up and move every thirty to forty-five minutes. Hip arthritis hates long sitting more than it hates walking.
  • Lie flat on your back for a few minutes daily, or on your stomach if comfortable, to let the front of the hip lengthen.
  • Keep walking on flat surfaces within comfort; shorter, more frequent walks are kinder to an irritable hip.
  • Sleep with a pillow between the knees if lying on your side hurts.

Outer hip pain with tenderness over the bony point is more often trochanteric bursitis or gluteal tendon pain. A deep pinch with sitting in younger adults suggests a labral tear. Buttock pain running down the leg is more likely sciatica or piriformis. The lumbar spine and SI joint refer to the hip region constantly. Inflammatory arthritis, hernias, hip stress fractures and, rarely, bone disease need a physician's evaluation when the pattern does not fit.

sections.h2: Hip arthritis and the Sarasota lifestyle
sections.html: Golf asks the lead hip to rotate inward, which is the motion arthritis takes first. Boating involves stepping over gunwales and balancing on one leg. Both are easier with a hip that has been released and glutes that are strong, and many patients here keep playing for years with the right maintenance program.

timeline: Hip osteoarthritis is long-term, but stiffness and groin pain commonly improve over several weeks of release and strengthening, and walking tolerance tends to grow steadily when the glute work is kept up.
redFlags: Hip or groin pain after a fall with inability to bear weight: possible fracture, seek emergency care.
A hot, swollen joint with fever or feeling unwell: possible infection, see a physician the same day.
Sudden severe hip pain in someone on long-term steroids or with a history of heavy alcohol use (possible bone collapse).
Night pain that does not change with position, unexplained weight loss, or a history of cancer.
Groin pain with a bulge that increases when coughing.

faq.q: Why does my knee hurt if the problem is my hip?
faq.a: The hip joint and the muscles around it share nerve pathways with the front of the thigh and knee, so hip arthritis frequently refers pain downward. A hip exam usually sorts it out.

faq.q: Can I avoid a hip replacement?
faq.a: Many people delay or avoid surgery by restoring motion and strengthening the glutes and trunk. When symptoms progress despite that, an orthopedic surgeon helps decide on timing.

faq.q: Is walking good or bad for hip arthritis?
faq.a: Walking within comfort is one of the best things for an arthritic hip. Problems come from long periods of sitting and from sudden big increases in activity.

faq.q: Does hands-on release help hip arthritis?
faq.a: It cannot change the joint surface, but releasing the hip flexors, TFL and glutes often improves rotation and reduces the groin ache noticeably.
